chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Sandal, from Abu Usamah, from Abu 'Abdillah (عليه السلام), who said:

Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali (عليه السلام) went out to Makkah one year walking, and his feet became swollen. Some of his mawali said to him, "If you were to ride, this swelling would subside from you." He said, "No. When we come to this stopping place, a black man will meet you, and he will have some oil with him, so buy it from him and do not haggle with him." His mawla said to him, "May my father and mother be for you, we have not come to any stopping place in which there is anyone selling this medicine." He said to him, "Yes, indeed, he is ahead of you before the stopping place."

So they travelled a mile, and there was the black man. Al-Hasan (عليه السلام) said to his mawla, "There is the man; take the oil from him and give him the price." The black man said, "O servant, for whom do you want this oil?" He said, "For Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali." He said, "Take me to him." So he went and brought him in to him. He said to him, "May my father and mother be for you, I did not know that you needed this. Do you think I would see that and still take a price for it? I am only your mawla. But supplicate to Allah that He grant me a sound male child who loves you, Ahl al-Bayt, for I left my wife in labor." He said, "Go to your home, for Allah has granted you a sound male child, and he is from our Shi'ah."

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ: the Household of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith about Imam al-Hasan (عليه السلام) and the black man with the oil teach about his virtue and the love of Ahl al-Bayt?
ai.summary: This report narrates an incident from the journey of Imam al-Hasan ibn 'Ali (عليه السلام) to Makkah, showing his foreknowledge of an upcoming encounter and his gracious conduct with a devoted follower. It also highlights the love of Ahl al-Bayt, the seeking of du'a from the Imam, and the glad tidings of a child counted among their Shi'ah.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ali Bin Al Nu’man, from Sandal, from Abu Asama, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ali<sup>asws</sup> went out to Makkah one year, walking. So his<sup>asws</sup> feet swelled up. So some of his<sup>asws</sup> slave said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘If only you<sup>asws</sup> were to ride, this would settle from you<sup>asws</sup>’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Never! When we come to this encampment, so a black man would welcome you and with him would be some oil. So buy it from him and do not haggle (for its price)’. So his<sup>asws</sup> slave said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May my father and my mother be (sacrificed) for you<sup>asws</sup>! There is no such encampment in front of us wherein there would be anyone selling this medicine’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘Yes, it is in front of you beside the encampment’.

So they travelled for a mile, and there was a black man. So Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> said to his<sup>asws</sup> slave: ‘Below you is the man, so take the oil from him and give him the price’. So the black man said, ‘O slave! For whom are you intending this oil?’ So he said, ‘For Al-Hasan<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ali<sup>asws</sup>’. So he said, ‘Come with me to him<sup>asws</sup>’. So he came over to him<sup>asws</sup> and said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘By my father and my mother being (sacrificed) for you<sup>asws</sup>! I did not know you<sup>asws</sup> were needy to this. Had I known that, I would not have taken a price for it. But rather, I am your<sup>asws</sup> slave. But, supplicate to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> that He<sup>azwj</sup> should Grace me a male child, healthy, who would be loving you<sup>asws</sup>, the People<sup>asws</sup> of the Household, for I left behind my wife, expecting’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Go to your house, so Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Endowed a healthy male child to you, and he is from our<sup>asws</sup> Shias’.
en.sarwar: 6. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Ni‘man from Sandal from abu ’Usama from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.

“One year al-Hassan ibn Ali left for Makka on foot. On the journey his feet swell and his servants said, “If you would ride the swelling will go away.” He said, “I will not do so up to the coming place for rest where you will a black person who has oil with him buy from oil without trying to reduce the price.” The servant said, “May Allah take my soul and the souls of my parents in service for your cause, we have never up to a place of rest where anyone would sell such medicine.” The Imam (a.s.) said to him, “Yes, there are such people right in front of you before reaching the place for rest.”

They walked for a mile and they met the black person. Al-Hassan (a.s.) said to his servant, “There is the man. Take the oil from him and pay him.” The blck man asked the servant, “For who do you want this oil?” He replied, “I want it for al-Hassan ibn Ali (a.s.).” He said, “Take me to him.” They came to the al-Hassan (a.s.) and the man said, May Allah take my soul and the souls of my parents in service for your cause. I did not know that you need this. If you would like tohave it you have it free of charges. I am only one your servants. Just pray for to Allah to grant me a healthy son who would love you, Ahl al-Bayt. When I left, my wife was about to give birth.” The Imam (a.s.) said, “Go to your place. Allah has gifted you with a healthy son who is of our Shi‘a (followers).”
